title: Parental Controls Checkup
intro: This one's for the grown-ups. Play it with your child, or solo — either way, you'll leave with a real setup checklist, not just good intentions.

questions.prompt: Your child plays Roblox. What's the single most important setting to check first?

choices.text: Account Restrictions + chat set to Friends Only
choices.coach: Exactly right — this is the single biggest lever for limiting stranger contact.
Graphics don't affect safety at all — settings do.
Friend count isn't the safety signal — chat and restriction settings are.

questions.prompt: Your child's Roblox chat looks clean when you check it. Does that mean everything is fine?

choices.text: Yes, clean chat means no risk
choices.coach: Many risky conversations happen in private in-experience channels or on linked Discord servers you haven't seen.

choices.text: Not necessarily — check for linked Discord servers too
choices.coach: Exactly. The visible chat is only part of the picture.

choices.text: Yes, as long as they're under 13
choices.coach: Age doesn't change what's visible — you still need to check beyond the obvious chat.

questions.prompt: What's the best way to find out which games your child actually plays?

choices.text: Ask them to list their favorites
choices.coach: Kids may only mention the games they think you'll approve of.

choices.text: Sit with them and watch for 10 minutes
choices.coach: The 10-minute rule: you'll learn more from watching than from asking.
Ratings don't reflect what's actually happening inside user-generated content.

questions.prompt: Your child receives an expensive in-game gift from someone they don't know in real life. What's the right response?

choices.text: Let them keep it, it's free after all
choices.coach: Unexpected gifts from strangers are a documented grooming tool — this deserves an immediate conversation.

choices.text: Treat it as a red flag and talk about it right away
choices.coach: Exactly right. Gifts create a sense of debt that predators exploit.

choices.text: Only worry if it happens more than once
choices.coach: Once is enough to warrant a conversation — don't wait for a pattern.

questions.prompt: Should children under 13 be on Discord?

choices.text: Yes, if it's linked to a game they already play
choices.coach: Discord has far fewer protections for minors regardless of how they got there.

choices.text: No — Discord under 13 is a hard no
choices.coach: Correct. If they're already on it, review the server list together and remove unreviewed servers.

choices.text: Only with a fake age set
choices.coach: A fake age doesn't add any real protection — the platform's actual protections don't apply.

questions.prompt: What's one setup step every family should do together, once a year?

choices.text: A 30-minute privacy + app settings reset, done together
choices.coach: Exactly — annual, brief, and collaborative beats a one-time lecture every time.
Restriction alone doesn't teach the underlying judgment kids need.
Apps and risks change — an annual check-in matters.
